title: COMP 4736 · Part 5
subtitle: System calls: interrupt classes, the procedure library, standard streams, x86 registers and int 80h, the eleven steps of read(), the POSIX tables, fork, execve and the shell, links and mount, Win32, blocking and non-blocking I/O
description: Part 5 of Rahim Oraji's lectures (Tanenbaum Ch. 1 §1.6 and lecture notes): external, internal and software interrupts; what a system call is and why C programs reach it through a procedure library; stdin, stdout and stderr as file descriptors 0, 1, 2 with the read/write demos; the x86 convention (number in EAX, arguments in EBX, ECX, …, int 80h, result in EAX) and the MIPS equivalent; the eleven steps of read(fd, buffer, nbytes) played step by step; the four POSIX tables verbatim; fork's three return values and every fork program on the slides with its real output; execve and the stripped-down shell; link, hard and symbolic links, mount; the UNIX-to-Win32 table; blocking, non-blocking and POSIX asynchronous I/O. Ends with a mock midterm section and the closed-book recall drill.
intro:
:::quiz What the exam asks here
Definitions and tables: which interrupt class a system call is, what each POSIX call returns (pid, fd, n, position, seconds, s = −1 on error), the Win32 name for fork + execve, the order of the eleven steps, and what a fork program prints. Learn the tables as tables: the recall drill asks for them blank.
:::
